claims.text: The baseline intermediate layer is a homogenous high-entropy alloy without secondary-phase additions.
The proposed intervention is addition of 1–2 wt.% nano-dispersed copper during powder-metallurgy processing.
Sintering and heat treatment can produce a uniform dispersion of the added copper in the high-entropy alloy.
Nano-dispersed copper will form a network along the grain boundaries of the high-entropy alloy matrix.
The copper grain-boundary network will form continuous high-conductivity pathways.
Copper has high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Copper channels along grain boundaries will reduce thermal resistance in the intermediate layer.
Reduced grain-boundary thermal resistance will increase the alloy's bulk heat-transfer capability.
The high-entropy alloy matrix will continue to provide mechanical strength after copper addition.
Using a nanoscale copper dispersion will minimize significant phase separation that could compromise structural integrity.
The copper-modified alloy will have higher bulk thermal conductivity than the copper-free baseline.
The copper-modified alloy will retain mechanical strength comparable to that of the copper-free baseline.
The copper-modified alloy will preserve structural integrity under reactor-relevant high-temperature and cyclic mechanical loading.
The proposed performance improvement will persist during long-term high-temperature cyclic loading typical of plasma-facing reactor operation.
